tasks.solutionSpace: closure of C6 plus five LOW findings within a fixed id set; no new ids, no envelope change
tasks.task:
Close these in r16; no id/envelope changes; blocker if impossible.
1 C6 HIGH irreversibility contradiction (R2 vs R5 retention): R2 promises a moved symlink entry's target is never touched and AC1-10(b) reads bytes through the moved link; R5 retention protects only this run's quarantine name and evicts pre-existing conforming files oldest-first by parsed timestamp. Counterexample: seed five conforming snapshot quarantines with corrupt regular file snapshot.corrupt-<oldest>.json oldest; make snapshot.json a relative symlink to that file; recovery moves the link entry to this run's quarantine name; retention then unlinks the oldest pre-existing file (the link's target), returning success with a dangling quarantine link and deleting the rejected bytes. No concurrency or injected failure is needed. Reconcile retention with symlink-backed evidence preservation without weakening preservation: protect the backing evidence (a quarantine pass must not unlink a file that a moved link entry in this run resolves to, including relative-link resolution semantics), explicitly resolve the resulting bound/order semantics across R2, R5, D10, section 4 step (3), section 8(2), AC1-3 and AC1-10 (state whether the bound may be exceeded, which candidate is skipped, and how old-first ordering proceeds past it), and add the fixture as a subcase under existing AC1-3 and AC1-10 with target-byte-preserved and quarantine-read-through assertions plus explicit survivor counts. Do not weaken AC1-10's target preservation to satisfy retention tests. This is a new symlink/retention interaction, not a C5 reopening. Note in section 9 that the configured non-OpenAI spec_critic_escalated reviewer is unavailable in this harness and the irreversible-deletion owner checkpoint remains open; do not treat this plan as that review or approval.
2 LOW provenance (CR15-01): section 9.7 still claims the ticket heading is a mirror of spec r14 with differing text; the observed input reads r15 and carries the tie-break, C5/D10 and resource.path pins. State the observed heading/body and drop the divergence claim.
3 LOW traceability (CR15-02): T1 lists AC1-1..AC1-10 but AC1-6's cmd TestEmitRecoveryRecords half is T3's and unreachable from T1's files. Scope T1 to the storage half and name T3 for the cmd half so no dual ownership remains on paper.
4 LOW anchors (CR15-03): T2 inputs/section 3 cite wiring.go:486-491 for an off-arm block spanning 486-494 with the remediation literal at 492, and log.go:224- though eventMessage starts at 228 (the default at 270-275 is inside the cited 270-275). Correct to wiring.go:486-494 and log.go:227-276.
5 LOW envelope shape (CR15-04): section 4 requires snapshot_unavailable kind=resource/retryable=true with the exact wiring.go remediation, but AC2-2 checks only error.code and T2 pins only state_directory. Add, under existing AC2-2, a four-field snapshot_unavailable ErrorInfo shape case in edge_test.go (validErrorInfo admits exact equality) so a wrong remediation cannot ship green.
6 LOW eviction multiplicity (CR15-05): AC1-3/1-5/1-6/1-8/1-9 use at most one excess, so evicting at most one per pass would pass all ACs and a backlog could stay above QuarantineKeep. Add a 6-seed (two-excess) subcase under existing AC1-3/AC1-9 asserting two evictions in one pass and a total of 5 (the second unlink remains a failure counterexample for over-deletion).
Return the full nine-section spec, unchanged ids, and a change log mapping each finding to its closing text.
